body_text: View all news Ripley Main Street Receives $100,000 Small Business Accelerator Grant From The Hartford July 28, 2026 Download PDF (opens in new window) RIPLEY, Miss., July 28, 2026 – Ripley Main Street has been awarded a $100,000 Small Business Accelerator Grant from The Hartford, in partnership with Main Street America. This grant will help develop Brown & Covington, a new small business accelerator site that will support local artisans, emerging entrepreneurs and workforce development opportunities in downtown Ripley. Brown & Covington will give artisans a place to create and sell products while receiving business support and mentorship. The site will also provide hands-on training in production and retail operations, helping participants build practical skills. “As a leading insurer of more than one million small businesses, The Hartford understands the vital role they serve in our communities, and we are proud to go beyond the policy to support their success” said Chris Jones, head of Small Business at The Hartford. “Through our partnership with Main Street America, we are helping remove barriers to growth by expanding access to flexible, affordable accelerator spaces where entrepreneurs can build experience, reach new customers and contribute to downtown revitalization.” “Access to affordable space and accessible education can make or break a new small business,” said Matt Wagner, Chief Innovation Officer at Main Street America. “The Hartford Small Business Accelerator Program is helping Main Streets remove those barriers in real, tangible ways – and in doing so, they’re building more resilient, opportunity-rich communities for everyone. Through this program, Main Street programs are identifying the kinds of support entrepreneurs need and creating spaces that further their district’s and community’s goals.” The program will launch with a cohort of six makers and support artisans working in pottery, jewelry, candles, skincare, woodworking, sewing and other handcrafted goods. It will also bring together local partners, including AbilityWorks, area high schools and heritage tourism organizations, to expand workforce development opportunities and strengthen the local small business ecosystem. “One of the things we love most at Ripley Main Street is looking at an overlooked building or space and imagining what it could become. Brown & Covington brings that vision to life. We're turning a long-vacant historic building into a place where artisans can launch businesses, build entrepreneurial skills, and connect with customers. Our community is full of talented makers, and we're excited to help them take that next step while creating opportunities for people of all abilities. Thanks to The Hartford and Main Street America, we're creating opportunities that will strengthen downtown Ripley for years to come”, said Elizabeth Behm, Executive Director, Ripley Main Street. Ripley Main Street’s grant is part of The Hartford's multiyear, $2 million Small Business Accelerator Grant Program with Main Street America, which supports 15 communities and approximately 1,500 small businesses nationwide. About Ripley Main Street Ripley Main Street is a nonprofit organization dedicated to building a vibrant downtown where small businesses, entrepreneurs, artisans, and the community can thrive. By transforming overlooked and vacant buildings into meaningful destinations, the organization is creating new opportunities for businesses to grow, artists and makers to share their talents, and residents and visitors to experience downtown Ripley in new ways. Guided by a long-term vision to preserve the city's historic character while fostering entrepreneurship and creativity, Ripley Main Street is helping shape a downtown known for its unique destinations, growing arts community, and support of local businesses. About Main Street America Main Street America (MSA) leads an inclusive, impact-driven movement dedicated to reenergizing and strengthening older and historic downtowns and neighborhood commercial districts through place-based economic development and community preservation. We work in collaboration with thousands of local partners and grassroots leaders across the nation who share our commitment to advancing shared prosperity, creating resilient economies, and improving quality of life. Main Street America was founded in 1980 as the National Main Street Center®, a program of the National Trust for Historic Preservation. Over the past 40 years the MSA network has helped to generate over $115.27 billion in local reinvestment, rehab 345,801 buildings, create 815,894 new jobs, and start 181,647 new businesses in over 2,000 communities. About The Hartford The Hartford is a leader in property and casualty insurance and employee benefits. By anticipating challenges and reducing risks our customers face, the company helps people and businesses thrive with confidence. Built on a foundation of trust, The Hartford is committed to strong performance, exceptional customer experiences and bold innovation, hallmarks of its sustained success since 1810. The Hartford Insurance Group, Inc., (NYSE: HIG) operates through its subsidiaries under the brand name, The Hartford, and is headquartered in Hartford, Connecticut. More information on the company and its financial performance is available on its website. For additional details, please read The Hartford’s legal notice . title: Understanding Rental Arbitrage: How to Profit from Short-Term Rentals
summary: MovingLake Blog - Understanding Rental Arbitrage: How to Profit from Short-Term Rentals
body_text: What is rental arbitrage? Rental arbitrage is a practice in which a property owner rents out their property on a short-term basis, typically through online vacation rental platforms like Airbnb, to generate higher rental income than they would through traditional renting. Essentially, the property owner is acting as a middleman, subletting their property to guests on a short-term basis in exchange for a higher rental price. This can be an attractive option for property owners who want to maximize their rental profits without committing to a long-term lease agreement with a traditional tenant. However, rental arbitrage is not without its challenges. Property owners who engage in rental arbitrage must be prepared to manage their rental property as if it were a full-time business, including marketing and promoting their listing, managing guest relations, and maintaining the property to ensure a positive experience for guests. In addition, rental arbitrage can be a legal gray area in some cities and jurisdictions, and property owners must ensure that they are complying with all relevant laws and regulations. Benefits of rental arbitrage for property owners One of the biggest benefits of rental arbitrage is the potential to generate significantly higher rental income than through traditional renting. By renting out your property on a short-term basis, you can charge a premium price that is often much higher than what you would earn through a long-term lease agreement. This can be particularly lucrative for property owners who have properties in desirable locations, such as popular vacation destinations or major cities with high demand for short-term rentals. Another benefit of rental arbitrage is the flexibility it provides. Unlike a traditional lease agreement, which can lock you into a long-term commitment with a single tenant, rental arbitrage allows you to rent out your property on a short-term basis and adjust your rental price and availability based on market demand. This can be particularly useful for property owners who want to maintain control over their rental property and adapt to changing market conditions. Risks and challenges of rental arbitrage While rental arbitrage can be a lucrative strategy for maximizing rental profits, it is not without its risks and challenges. One of the biggest challenges of rental arbitrage is the need to manage your rental property as if it were a full-time business. This can include everything from marketing and promoting your listing, to managing guest relations, to maintaining the property to ensure a positive experience for guests. Another challenge of rental arbitrage is the legal gray area in which it operates. Some cities and jurisdictions have strict regulations governing short-term rentals, and property owners who engage in rental arbitrage must ensure that they are complying with all relevant laws and regulations. Failure to do so can result in fines, legal action, and even the loss of your rental property. Rental arbitrage vs traditional renting - pros and cons When deciding whether rental arbitrage is the right strategy for your property, it's important to consider the pros and cons of this approach compared to traditional renting. One of the biggest advantages of rental arbitrage is the potential to generate higher rental income than through traditional renting. However, this comes with the added challenge of managing your rental property as a full-time business, including marketing and promotion, guest relations, and property maintenance. Another advantage of rental arbitrage is the flexibility it provides. Unlike traditional renting, which typically requires a long-term lease agreement with a single tenant, rental arbitrage allows you to adjust your rental price and availability based on market demand. This can be particularly useful for property owners who want to maintain control over their rental property and adapt to changing market conditions. However, rental arbitrage comes with its own set of challenges, including the need to manage your rental property as a full-time business, the legal gray area in which it operates, and the potential for higher turnover and wear and tear on your property. Ultimately, the decision of whether to pursue rental arbitrage or traditional renting depends on your individual situation and goals as a property owner. Finding the right property for rental arbitrage One of the first steps in pursuing rental arbitrage is finding the right property to rent out on a short-term basis. When searching for a property to rent, it's important to consider factors like location, size, and amenities that will make your property attractive to potential guests. Ideally, you want to find a property that is in a desirable location and has features that are in high demand among vacation rental guests, such as a pool, beach access, or a fully equipped kitchen. Another important factor to consider when searching for a rental arbitrage property is the cost of rent. In order to generate a profit through rental arbitrage, you need to be able to charge a rental price that is significantly higher than your monthly rent payment. This means that you need to find a property with a low enough rent payment to allow for a profitable rental price. Once you have identified a potential rental arbitrage property, it's important to thoroughly research the property and the surrounding area to ensure that it is a good fit for short-term rentals. This can include checking local vacation rental regulations, researching the competition in the area, and evaluating the property's potential for attracting guests. Furnishing and decorating your rental arbitrage property Once you have secured a rental arbitrage property, the next step is to furnish and decorate the property in a way that is attractive to potential guests. This can include everything from selecting comfortable and stylish furniture, to choosing attractive decor and accessories, to stocking the property with all the essentials that guests will need during their stay. When decorating your rental arbitrage property, it's important to strike a balance between style and functionality. While you want your property to look attractive and welcoming to guests, you also need to ensure that it is practical and functional for short-term rentals. This means selecting durable furniture and decor that can withstand the wear and tear of multiple guests, as well as providing all the necessary amenities and supplies that guests will need during their stay. Another important consideration when furnishing and decorating your rental arbitrage property is the cost. While you want to create an attractive and comfortable space for guests, you also need to be mindful of your budget and the potential for return on investment. This means selecting furnishings and decor that are both cost-effective and attractive to potential guests. Setting the right rental price for your arbitrage property One of the key factors in maximizing your rental profits through arbitrage is setting the right rental price for your property. This means finding a balance between charging a price that is high enough to generate a profit, but not so high that it discourages potential guests from booking. When setting your rental price, it's important to consider factors like the location and amenities of your property, as well as the competition in the area. You can research other vacation rental listings in your area to get an idea of what other hosts are charging for similar properties, and adjust your price accordingly. In addition, you may want to consider offering discounts or special promotions to attract guests during low-demand periods or to encourage longer stays. Another important consideration when setting your rental price is the potential for variable pricing based on market demand. By adjusting your rental price based on factors like seasonality, special events, and local demand, you can maximize your rental profits and ensure that your property is always in high demand. Marketing and promoting your rental arbitrage property Once you have furnished and decorated your rental arbitrage property and set your rental price, the next step is to market and promote your listing to potential guests. This can include everything from optimizing your listing for search engine visibility, to creating attractive photos and descriptions, to leveraging social media and other marketing channels to reach a wider audience. When optimizing your listing for search engine visibility, it's important to use keywords and phrases that are relevant to your property and the surrounding area. This can help your listing appear higher in search engine results, and attract more potential guests to your listing. In addition, you may want to consider using paid advertising or other marketing channels to reach a wider audience and promote your listing to potential guests. Another important aspect of marketing and promoting your rental arbitrage property is creating attractive photos and descriptions that showcase your property's best features and amenities. This can include everything from high-quality photos of the property and surrounding area, to a detailed description of the property's amenities and features, to positive guest reviews and testimonials. Managing and maintaining your rental arbitrage property Once you have started renting out your property on a short-term basis, the next step is to manage and maintain your rental property to ensure a positive experience for guests and maximize your rental profits. This can include everything from responding to guest inquiries and requests, to ensuring that the property is clean and well-maintained between guest stays, to addressing any issues or concerns that may arise during a guest's stay. When managing and maintaining your rental arbitrage property, it's important to be responsive and attentive to guest needs and concerns. This can help to ensure that guests have a positive experience and are more likely to leave positive reviews and recommend your property to others. In addition, you may want to consider hiring a property management company or service to help you manage and maintain your rental property, particularly if you have multiple properties or are not able to manage the property on a full-time basis. Finally, it's important to be proactive about addressing any issues or concerns that may arise during a guest's stay. This can include everything from addressing maintenance issues, to handling noise complaints, to resolving disputes with guests. By being proactive and responsive, you can help to ensure that your guests have a positive experience and are more likely to recommend your property to others. Legal considerations for rental arbitrage When engaging in rental arbitrage, it's important to be aware of the legal considerations and regulations that apply to short-term rentals in your area. Some cities and jurisdictions have strict regulations governing short-term rentals, including limits on the number of days that a property can be rented out, zoning restrictions, and licensing and registration requirements. In addition, there may be other legal considerations to keep in mind when engaging in rental arbitrage, such as liability insurance, taxes, and other legal obligations. It's important to research and understand the legal requirements and regulations that apply to short-term rentals in your area, and ensure that you are complying with all relevant laws and regulations. Case studies of successful rental arbitrage properties To get a better sense of how rental arbitrage can be used to maximize rental profits, let's take a look at some case studies of successful rental arbitrage properties. Case Study 1 : Beachfront Condo in Miami One property owner in Miami, Florida was able to generate nearly double the rental income by renting out their beachfront condo on a short-term basis through Airbnb. By charging a premium price for the condo's prime location and desirable amenities, the property owner was able to generate significantly higher rental income than they would have through a traditional lease agreement. Case Study 2 : Luxury Apartment in New York City Another property owner in New York City was able to generate significantly higher rental income by renting out their luxury apartment on a short-term basis through Airbnb. By optimizing their listing for search engine visibility, offering competitive pricing, and providing exceptional guest experiences, the property owner was able to attract a steady stream of guests and generate consistent rental income throughout the year. Case Study 3 : Vacation Home in Hawaii A third property owner in Hawaii was able to maximize their rental profits by renting out their vacation home on a short-term basis through Airbnb. By offering a unique and attractive rental experience, including personalized welcome gifts and a concierge service, the property owner was able to generate enthusiastic guest reviews and repeat business, resulting in higher rental income and a steady stream of bookings throughout the year. Conclusion Rental arbitrage can be a highly effective strategy for maximizing rental profits and generating higher rental income than through traditional renting. However, it is not without its challenges and risks, and property owners must be prepared to manage their rental property as if it were a full-time business in order to succeed. By following the tips and strategies outlined in this guide, property owners can optimize their rental arbitrage efforts and take their rental profits to the next level. So whether you're a seasoned property owner or just getting started in the rental game, rental arbitrage may be the perfect solution for maximizing your rental profits and achieving your financial goals. ‍

title: Inspección del primer artículo (FAI) para producir piezas de calidad uniformes rápidamente
summary: Utilizar la fabricación digital —que puede incluir procesos de moldeo científico— en combinación con métodos específicos de garantía y control de calidad, para producir piezas de forma rápida y uniforme.
body_text: Los fabricantes utilizan medidas de control de calidad de muchas maneras para alcanzar los altos estándares exigidos para determinadas piezas. Se requieren inspecciones, pruebas y, en ocasiones, incluso medidas correctivas para eliminar defectos y validar que las piezas sean uniformes entre tiradas y que además sean seguras, funcionen según lo esperado y cumplan con la normativa, independientemente de la industria. Usamos procesos de fabricación digital que pueden comprender procesos de moldeo científico, combinados con métodos específicos de control y garantía de calidad, para producir piezas de forma rápida y uniforme. Nuestro proceso estándar de elaboración de presupuestos incluye un análisis de diseño para fabricabilidad (DFM), un primer paso para garantizar la calidad de las piezas moldeadas. Medimos hasta cuatro dimensiones entre planos y de diámetros exteriores basándonos en su modelo CAD (X, Y, Z) según las tolerancias indicadas en el presupuesto. Además de nuestro proceso estándar, ofrecemos una amplia variedad de opciones de medición de calidad, inspección y documentación para garantizar unos estándares rigurosos en la entrega de piezas moldeadas por inyección de alta calidad. Entre las opciones de informes de inspección se encuentran métodos de medición tales como nuestra inspección del primer artículo (FAI) parcial, el proceso de aprobación de piezas de producción (PPAP), la inspección crítica para la calidad (CTQ) e informes de inspección digital (DIR), disponibles en el momento de la compra. Esta entrada de blog analiza con más detalle el primero de ellos, la FAI para piezas moldeadas. Como siempre, puede consultar con uno de nuestros expertos en moldeo por inyección para decidir qué opciones de inspección se adaptan mejor a las necesidades de su proyecto. ¿Qué es la FAI? La inspección del primer artículo (FAI) consiste en una inspección de calidad de las piezas realizada con equipos de medición calibrados o certificados que evalúan una o varias piezas seleccionadas de forma aleatoria al inicio de una tirada de producción. De este modo, se garantiza que las piezas cumplan las especificaciones del cliente. La FAI surgió durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial como respuesta a la demanda de precisión y uniformidad en la fabricación de productos aeroespaciales y de defensa. Desde entonces, la FAI ha integrado innovaciones tecnológicas clave, incluidas herramientas digitales y de software, como el diseño asistido por ordenador y la fabricación asistida por ordenador (CAD y CAM), que han supuesto un avance significativo en la forma de realizar las inspecciones. Hoy en día, dependiendo del fabricante, el número de piezas y dimensiones medidas puede variar. Realizamos una FAI parcial, que permite medir hasta 10 piezas y 25 dimensiones, evaluando normalmente aquellas piezas críticas que son clave para el funcionamiento del producto o que han sido modificadas desde la última inspección. Se denomina FAI parcial porque algunos fabricantes inspeccionan más piezas, dimensiones y requisitos adicionales, aunque esos procesos de evaluación requieren mucho más tiempo. Como fabricante digital, trabajamos con empresas que acuden a nosotros en busca de una producción de entrega rápida. Como resultado, nos comprometemos a agilizar la producción de las piezas de los clientes. Nuestro proceso de FAI garantiza la rapidez y, al mismo tiempo, asegura la calidad y la uniformidad de las piezas. ¿Cómo es el proceso de FAI? En general, el proceso de FAI comprende varios pasos, varía según el fabricante y puede implicar una serie de elementos, como revisiones del diseño, definición del alcance de una inspección, documentación de los resultados y otros aspectos. Comenzamos definiendo el alcance del proceso de inspección mediante la creación de una Declaración de trabajo de inspección (ISOW). A continuación, creamos o preparamos los accesorios, herramientas y equipos de inspección necesarios, como medidores y máquinas de medición por coordenadas (MMC), todos ellos certificados o calibrados para lograr mediciones precisas. Las piezas seleccionadas para la evaluación de la FAI se inspeccionan y, tras ese paso, documentamos los resultados de la inspección. Téngase en cuenta: si un cliente desea más de lo que ofrece nuestra FAI parcial, trabajamos con un colaborador de inspección de confianza. Pregunte a su ingeniero de aplicaciones de Protolabs sobre otras posibilidades adicionales de inspección. ¿Qué industrias utilizan la FAI? La mayoría de las industrias utilizan algún nivel de FAI como opción de inspección, además de otros métodos de garantía de calidad disponibles. Recibimos muchas solicitudes de los sectores de la automoción, aeroespacial, sanitario y de electrónica de consumo. La industria de la automoción utiliza frecuentemente la FAI, especialmente cuando introduce nuevas piezas o realiza cambios de diseño u otras modificaciones en las piezas existentes. El sector aeroespacial requiere una FAI para cada nueva pieza o ensamblaje antes de comenzar la fabricación. Para el sector sanitario , la FAI es fundamental para cumplir con las normas de conformidad. Fuentes del sector aseguran que puede ayudar a las empresas de tecnologías médicas y productos sanitarios a cumplir los requisitos normativos y, en general, a garantizar la calidad, la seguridad y el cumplimiento normativo. Las empresas de electrónica de consumo recurren a la FAI antes de la producción en serie de nuevos productos para asegurarse de que se cumplen todas las especificaciones y validar que todos los componentes y ensamblajes funcionan según lo previsto. ¿Cuáles son las ventajas de utilizar la FAI? Algunas de las ventajas más destacadas de solicitar la FAI a Protolabs son: Rapidez Es la principal ventaja. Con la automatización detrás de todos nuestros procesos y capacidades, la FAI en Protolabs permite un método de FAI eficiente, donde las inspecciones de características críticas se completan en un breve tiempo, sin afectar al tiempo de producción de una pieza. Nuestro proceso permite obtener piezas de calidad uniformes rápidamente, lo que nos lleva a la siguiente ventaja. Uniformidad La evaluación de la FAI en Protolabs verifica la uniformidad de las piezas entre tiradas. Pruebas de cumplimiento de los requisitos La FAI ayuda a las empresas en el cumplimiento normativo, reglamentario y de otros estándares. La evaluación de la FAI, a través de su documentación, incluye pruebas de dicho cumplimiento. Detección temprana de defectos en las piezas Realizar inspecciones al inicio de un ciclo de producción puede ayudar a nuestros clientes a volver atrás y repetir diseños alternativos para que la pieza sea fabricable. Ahorrar dinero, reducir los residuos En relación con la detección temprana de defectos mediante la identificación de problemas potenciales de diseño u otros problemas en las primeras fases de la producción, la FAI puede ahorrar dinero y recursos y reducir los residuos. ¿Cuáles son los desafíos habituales de la FAI? Los diseñadores e ingenieros de productos pueden enfrentarse a numerosos desafíos en los procesos de inspección en general: complejidad de las piezas, complejidad de la documentación, limitaciones de tiempo tales como cumplir los plazos de producción, gestión de los cambios (abordar cambios de diseño o especificaciones durante las fases de producción), etc. Nuestros procesos y capacidades automatizados han resuelto muchos de estos desafíos. Por ejemplo, nuestro sistema de software de ejecución de fabricación (MES) patentado puede resultar especialmente útil para resolver problemas de limitaciones de tiempo, desafíos de gestión de cambios y costes generales. En última instancia, las empresas recurren a Protolabs para obtener prototipos rápidos y acelerar la fabricación a lo largo del ciclo de vida del producto. En consecuencia, nuestros procesos de inspección reflejan ese planteamiento de respuesta rápida, completando las inspecciones de las piezas en un breve tiempo, sin que afecte a su tiempo de producción, calidad y uniformidad; en otras palabras, producimos piezas de calidad uniformes rápidamente. body_text: Tempus Announces National Launch of OneOme Pharmacogenomics Testing, Advancing Patient Safety and Precision Medicine July 22, 2026 PDF Version CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 22, 2026-- Tempus AI, Inc. (NASDAQ: TEM), a technology company leading the adoption of AI to advance precision medicine and patient care, today announced the national launch of its OneOme pharmacogenomics (PGx) testing solution, delivering advanced genetic insights to optimize medication safety, dosing and toxicity risk assessment. Following its acquisition of OneOme in November 2025, Tempus has fully integrated these capabilities to expand its comprehensive precision medicine portfolio, bridging a critical gap between genomic tumor profiling and how a patient's body actually processes treatment. "Answering the urgent demand for immediate, reliable medication safety insights is a clinical imperative, particularly in oncology care," said Tom Schoenherr, CEO of Diagnostics at Tempus. “By bringing OneOme’s robust pharmacogenomics platform into the Tempus ecosystem and offering both rapid single-gene and broad multi-gene panels, we are providing clinicians with a more holistic view of the patient and actively closing this safety gap.” The national launch introduces OneOme’s flagship RightMed® Comprehensive test, a 27-gene germline PGx laboratory developed test designed to analyze a patient’s inherited genetic traits, alongside standalone single-gene DPYD and UGT1A1 testing. These options evaluate how a patient’s unique genetic profile may influence their response, toxicity risk or optimal dosage across a broad spectrum of therapies. Recent FDA labeling updates recommend DPYD testing prior to administering common fluoropyrimidine therapies1— treatments where nearly 30% of patients experience severe, and sometimes fatal, toxicities2. Whether providers order the comprehensive 27-gene panel or the targeted single-gene assays, the testing provides a rapid turnaround time, delivering results in under 5 days on average from sample receipt. This testing solution is seamlessly integrated into the broader Tempus ecosystem, allowing clinicians to evaluate drug-gene interactions alongside both tissue and liquid biopsy sequencing directly at the point of care. About Tempus Tempus is a technology company advancing precision medicine through the practical application of artificial intelligence in healthcare. With one of the world’s largest libraries of multimodal data, and an operating system to make that data accessible and useful, Tempus provides AI-enabled precision medicine solutions to physicians to deliver personalized patient care and in parallel facilitates discovery, development and delivery of optimal therapeutics. The goal is for each patient to benefit from the treatment of others who came before by providing physicians with tools that learn as the company gathers more data. title: Dilmar Oil: The 90-Year-Old Distributor That Reclaims Its Own Oil
summary: Dilmar Oil Company made MDM's 2025 Top Distributors list in Lubricants & Fuels. Here is how a 90-year-old family jobber built a closed-loop reclamation business.
body_text: Part of Distributor Playbooks — strategy teardowns of every company on the 2025 MDM Top Distributors lists . Dilmar Oil Company shows up on MDM's 2025 Top Distributors list in the Lubricants & Fuels category, one of the smaller and less-covered names in that vertical. It has also been in continuous, private, family operation since 1932. That combination is rarer than it sounds in a distribution sector that big oil majors and private equity have spent three decades consolidating, and it is the reason Dilmar is worth a longer look than its size alone would suggest. Two counties and a Depression-era bet The name is a contraction, not a founder's surname. R.E. Atkinson and M.H. Cox started the business in 1932 to sell Shell products across Dillon and Marion counties in South Carolina, and they fused the county names into "Dilmar" rather than branding it after themselves, according to the company's own history page . Fourteen years later, in 1946, the Atkinson family bought out the partnership and became sole owners, a transition the company still marks as the real founding moment of its family-ownership story. Robert Earle Atkinson Jr., who ran the company from the mid-20th century until his death in 2015, is the figure Dilmar credits with shaping its current footprint: a Shell jobber that grew, county by county, into a multi-state lubricants distributor without ever taking on outside ownership. That is the through-line worth naming plainly: in a vertical where independent oil jobbers have been rolled up into regional platforms and private-equity-backed groups for a generation, Dilmar has stayed a single family's business for going on 80 years since that 1946 buyout. From selling oil to owning the whole loop Most lubricants distributors make their margin once, when the drum or tote leaves the warehouse. Dilmar built a second business on the other end of that same transaction. Dilmar Fluid Services (DFS) reclaims used industrial oil, filtering turbine oil, hydraulic fluid, gear oil and cutting oils back into usable condition on customer sites, and the company's own materials describe the economics bluntly: reclaimed fluid running 40 to 60 percent cheaper than virgin oil , with some industrial accounts cutting new-oil purchases by as much as 90 percent. That is the unique wrinkle in Dilmar's model. A conventional distributor's incentive is volume: sell more virgin product, move more gallons. A reclamation business's incentive is the opposite: keep a customer's existing fluid in service longer and sell them less new oil per unit of output. Dilmar runs both businesses out of the same branches, using four portable reclamation units and one stationary facility that has operated in this capacity for close to two decades per the company's about-us page . Rather than treat that as a conflict, Dilmar has folded reclamation into a broader Industrial Reliability Management offering, so the sales conversation isn't "how many drums do you need" but "how do we manage your total fluid cost." For an industrial account, that reframes Dilmar from vendor to lifecycle partner, which is a stickier and harder-to-replace position than being the low-price drum supplier. The footprint behind the pitch None of that works without physical infrastructure, and Dilmar's is substantial for a company its size: eight bulk plants, more than 40 bulk and packaging trucks, roughly 1 million gallons of bulk storage and 125,000 square feet of package warehousing spread across seven branch locations in South Carolina, North Carolina and Georgia, plus a newer Knoxville, Tennessee location that extends the network into a fourth state, according to the company's service-locations pages . That is the classic distribution moat: branch density and bulk storage close enough to customers that reclamation trucks and lubricant deliveries can share routes and relationships. A quiet answer to industry consolidation Here's the tension worth sitting with. Family ownership over 90 years is a genuine asset. It buys patience for a reclamation business that took years to pay off, and it buys credibility with the industrial accounts that value a distributor who answers the phone the same way for decades. But it also means Dilmar has grown organically inside a four-state Southeastern footprint while sitting in a vertical where scale increasingly comes from acquisition. MDM's own lists are populated with lubricants and fuels distributors that got large by buying peers; Dilmar's path has been to go deeper in fewer states and add adjacent services rather than add geography by roll-up. That is a defensible strategy as long as reclamation and reliability management keep differentiating the pitch. It is a harder one if a better-capitalized competitor decides to build the same closed-loop service at a scale Dilmar's organic growth model can't match quickly. Ninety-plus years in, Dilmar's bet is that owning both ends of the oil's life, the sale and the reclamation, is worth more than owning more zip codes. It is a bet that has outlasted a lot of distributors who chose differently. Distribution has always run on unglamorous fundamentals: what's in the branch, what's in the tank, and whether the truck shows up. Dilmar's version of that discipline just happens to include the oil coming back out the door as well as the oil going in.
